## Source-grounded content decision

- Reader question: when an AgentSight process EXIT event reports exit_code=0, did the process or AI agent actually succeed?
- Primary source pin: v1.0.35 product commit c1574366...; bpf/process.bpf.c, bpf/process.c, bpf/README.md and collector/src/cmd_exec.rs, plus Linux wait(2). The BPF exit hook extracts the high status byte using (task exit_code >> 8) & 0xff and does not preserve the WIFEXITED / WIFSIGNALED distinction in the JSON field. Illustrative wait-style words 0x0700 and 0x000f yield 7 and 0; this is a source-only demonstration, not a live capture.
- Additional source-specific limits: minimum-duration filter can suppress EXEC output; EXIT duration is optional, non-leader thread exits are ignored; process-tracker scope, lifetime filter and ring-buffer reservations can omit rows. EXEC command information is bounded. The article provides a nine-case evidence-versus-inference matrix and a reproducible static inspection command; no workload benchmark or live sample is claimed.
- Semantic overlap: existing file-open evidence page answers successful file-open semantics; capture-loss article answers TLS/ringbuffer gaps; audit provenance article answers source lineage; agent PR review use case answers human acceptance workflow. None owns process termination-status decoding or process versus tool versus agent-task outcome. Thus the new canonical /blog/what-agentsight-process-exit-codes-mean/ addresses a distinct decision and cross-links those existing owners.
- Narrow rendered scope: one TechArticle, first Blog index card and CollectionPage entry, exactly one sitemap URL, updated Blog date; no shared routes, analytics source, workflows, or dependencies changed. Rollback point main 4a771124f368a2babe5f52229a542a8c0a9fffc1. Public acceptance: new canonical body has one H1, TechArticle, version/source links, nine cases, presence in Blog/sitemap; homepage, Product, Security and older technical articles remain unchanged.
